title: The Fighter: Who Calls the Shots?
narrativeQuestion: Who should control Micky Ward's career, and what does the film show us about that power?

chapters.title: The city behind the fighter
chapters.claim: Industrial job loss helps explain the economic pressures surrounding a boxing career.

chapters.title: The real brothers
chapters.claim: Actors portray people with lives beyond the film.

chapters.title: Three moments to watch
chapters.claim: Money, public storytelling and family influence create distinct pressures on an athlete.

chapters.title: After the film: check the record
chapters.claim: A dramatized film compresses time and reframes historical events.

chapters.title: Make your call
chapters.claim: A defensible judgment needs specific film evidence and a serious counterargument.

accuracyNotes: Film still identifies Mark Wahlberg and Christian Bale as actors, not the actual brothers.
Lowell photographs show preserved mills today, not the city in 1993.
Lowell mill employment figures are textile employment in 1895 and 1936, not population or 1990s unemployment.
Replacement-bout pressure is explicitly film analysis, not a claim that the movie reproduces the historical Mungin bout accurately.
The documentary title in the film differs from the real 1995 documentary.
Sanchez in 1997 and Neary in 2000 were separated by six Ward bouts.
Ward won the WBU light welterweight title, not an undisputed championship.
No invented numerical family outcomes or claims that toughness makes injury safe.
